3.2. Canonical bases on modified $\imath$ quantum groups

Following [55, IV], we can define a modified $\imath$ quantum group $\dot{\textbf{U}}^{\imath}$ (an associative $\mathbb{Q}(q)$ -algebra structure without unit) such that $\dot{\textbf{U}}^{\imath}=\bigoplus_{\lambda\in X_{\imath}}{\textbf{U}}^{\imath}\mathbf{1}_{\lambda}$; see [10]. In contrast to quantum groups, the $\mathcal{A}$ -form of $\dot{\textbf{U}}^{\imath}$ is far from being obvious (even in rank 1).

For $\lambda,\mu\in X^{+}$ and $w\in W$, denoting $\eta_{\lambda}^{\bullet}:=\eta_{w_{\bullet}\lambda}$, we introduce the following U-submodule:

$\displaystyle L^{\imath}(\lambda,\mu):=\textbf{U}(\eta_{w_{\bullet}\lambda}\otimes\eta_{\mu})\subset L(\lambda)\otimes L(\mu),$

which can be shown to be a based U-module and hence admits an $\imath$ canonical basis by Theorem 3.1. Let $\zeta=w_{\bullet}\lambda+\mu$ and $\zeta_{\imath}=\overline{\zeta}$. The following hold [9, 10]:

$\triangleright$ The $\imath$ canonical basis of $L^{\imath}(\lambda,\mu)$ is of the form $\textbf{B}^{\imath}(\lambda,\mu)=\big\{(b_{1}\diamondsuit_{\zeta_{\imath}}b_{2})_{w_{\bullet}\lambda,\mu}^{\imath}|(b_{1},b_{2})\in\textbf{B}_{\mathbb{I}_{\bullet}}\times\textbf{B}\big\}\backslash\{0\}$, where $(b_{1}\diamondsuit_{\zeta_{\imath}}b_{2})_{w_{\bullet}\lambda,\mu}^{\imath}$ is $\psi_{\imath}$ -invariant and lies in

$(b_{1}\diamondsuit_{\zeta}b_{2})(\eta_{\lambda}^{\bullet}\otimes\eta_{\mu})+\!\!\!\sum_{|b_{1}^{\prime}|+|b_{2}^{\prime}|\leq|b_{1}|+|b_{2}|}\!\!\!v^{-1}{\mathbb{Z}}[v^{-1}](b^{\prime}_{1}\diamondsuit_{\zeta}b^{\prime}_{2})(\eta_{\lambda}^{\bullet}\otimes\eta_{\mu}).$

$\triangleright$ We have a projective system $\big\{L^{\imath}(\lambda+\nu^{\tau},\mu+\nu)\big\}_{\nu\in X^{+}}$ of ${\textbf{U}}^{\imath}$ -modules, where

$\pi_{\nu+\nu_{1},\nu_{1}}:L^{\imath}(\lambda+\nu^{\tau}+\nu_{1}^{\tau},\mu+\nu+\nu_{1})\longrightarrow L^{\imath}(\lambda+\nu^{\tau},\mu+\nu),\quad\nu,\nu_{1}\in X^{+},$

is the unique homomorphism of ${\textbf{U}}^{\imath}$ -modules mapping $\eta^{\bullet}_{\lambda+\nu^{\tau}+\nu_{1}^{\tau}}\otimes\eta_{\mu+\nu+\nu_{1}}$ to $\eta^{\bullet}_{\lambda+\nu^{\tau}}\otimes\eta_{\mu+\nu}.$ The $K$ -matrix [8] [3] [9] plays a role here.

The following theorem generalizes [55, Chap. 25]. For quantum symmetric pairs of diagonal type in Example 0.1 or a trivial pair $(\textbf{U},\textbf{U})$, it reduces to Lusztig’s setting.
card.label: Theorem 3.1

paper.title: Quantum symmetric pairs
paper.abstract: This is a survey of some recent progress on quantum symmetric pairs and applications. The topics include quasi K-matrices, $\imath$Schur duality, canonical bases, super Kazhdan-Lusztig theory, $\imath$Hall algebras, current presentations for affine $\imath$quantum groups, and braid group actions.
